open_questions: Respect's "sock it to me" (record bars 57-58): the one human tab leaves both bars empty; the record's drums play through them, and they are written as the vamp's groove. Transcribe them from the record.
When a Man Loves a Woman's bridge: the tab writes the ride in dotted eighths, but the record's cymbals repeat on the triplet; checked by autocorrelation only. Listen on headphones.
I Never Loved a Man: the tab writes a 3/4 shuffle and its rolls as ten notes to a bar; set here as 9/8 with nine triplets to the roll. Is the record in three, or a 12/8 the tab misbarred?

Land of 1000 Dances, Think, Tell Mama, Respect Yourself and I'll Take You There have only machine-made or machine-drafted drum tabs; Kodachrome's human tab changes meter and runs short of the record. Each wants a human transcription.
His kit at FAME beyond "most of the time it was Ludwig": sizes, cymbals and the snare are not in the sources read.

identity.name: Roger Hawkins

evidence.note: After a long illness, at home, aged 75.

Hired at FAME in 1964 (Muscle Shoals Rhythm Section article); the first well-documented session, Land of a Thousand Dances, May 1966; Muscle Shoals Sound from April 1969, sold in 1985, after which he worked on as a session player, the end year approximate.

identity.summary: The drummer of FAME Studios from the mid-1960s and of the Muscle Shoals Rhythm Section, the Swampers, who founded Muscle Shoals Sound in 1969: Percy Sledge's When a Man Loves a Woman, Wilson Pickett's Mustang Sally and Land of 1000 Dances, Aretha Franklin's first Atlantic records, the Staple Singers, Paul Simon, Bob Seger. A deep, unhurried pocket: the hat with one note opened, a dynamic snare, the kick moving with the bass, the drums tuned and taped to the song, and no tom fills under the singer. "I was always a better listener than I was a drummer."

traditions.impact: "Al Jackson was a big influence. I listened to him a lot."
Studied Dave Brubeck's Take Five and Ernie K-Doe's Mother-in-Law; jazz technique from Mike Shepherd.

formative_events.event: Hired by Rick Hall at FAME Studios, Muscle Shoals.
April 1969: founded Muscle Shoals Sound at 3614 Jackson Highway, Sheffield, with Jimmy Johnson, Barry Beckett and David Hood.

eras.label: FAME and Quinvy, 1966-1969
eras.context: Rick Hall's FAME Studios and Quin Ivy's Norala studio: Percy Sledge, Wilson Pickett, Etta James, Clarence Carter, and Aretha Franklin's first Atlantic session in January 1967, followed to New York.
defining_traits: the hat with one note opened
no tom fills under the singer

eras.label: Muscle Shoals Sound, 1969-1985
eras.context: The Swampers' own studio at 3614 Jackson Highway, then 1000 Alabama Avenue from 1979: the Staple Singers, Paul Simon, Bob Seger, Rod Stewart, Bob Dylan; Traffic on the road in 1973.
eras.style_shift: From the house band to owners and producers; drums tuned to each song and taped down, a dry 1970s sound.

evidence.note: Modern Drummer's "unshakable time, southern-infused deep pocket"; no source measures it.

swing.notes: Straight on the uptempo records; the ballad in 12/8 and I Never Loved a Man a shuffle in three.

dynamics.balance: A cracking snare over a quiet hat; the kick with the bass.

feel_profile.interaction: Four players who knew each other's moves: "when the four of us sit down to play, it's almost like a burden has been lifted"; the arrangement built in the room.

hand_techniques.name: The hat with one note opened
hand_techniques.description: Eighths on the hat with the "and" of 3 (Mustang Sally, Old Time Rock and Roll) or of 4 (Respect) opened in every bar; the Encyclopedia of Alabama's "high-hat inflections".

hand_techniques.name: Snare rolls into the section
hand_techniques.description: A roll in sixteenth triplets on the last pulse into each verse of When a Man Loves a Woman; sixteenths on the snare over the kick into Old Time Rock and Roll's choruses.

foot_techniques.name: The kick with the bass
foot_techniques.description: The kick on 1, the "and" of 3 and the "and" of 4 (Mustang Sally), on 1, 3 and its "and" (Respect, Chain of Fools), on every beat (Old Time Rock and Roll): "syncopated bass drum work".

devices_search.note: None found. His parts are grooves held with the band, the ballad in 12/8 and a shuffle in three; no cross-rhythm, metric modulation or displacement in the tabs or sources read.

sound_profile.cymbal_character: The hat carries the songs; a crash on a section's 1; the ride for solos and vamps.

by_era.description: A Ludwig at FAME, tuned to the singer and taped where his finger found the ring.
The dry, damped 1970s sound of Muscle Shoals Sound; Kodachrome's "loping" part on a box stuffed with newspaper, played with vibes mallets.

sample_hints.60s: A 1960s Ludwig, the snare cracking, taped down, the room small.
sample_hints.70s: Dry and close, the toms damped.

signature_traits.label: No tom fills under the singer
signature_traits.description: "Don't be doing tom-tom fills when the singer's singing": the fills fall in the gaps, a snare roll or a bar of tom into the chorus, and the groove holds through the verse.

signature_traits.label: The arrangement first
signature_traits.description: "His adherence to the arrangement of the song": the band's stops and hits played with them, as in Mustang Sally's stop before each chorus and Respect's refrain hits.

signature_traits.label: Drums tuned to the song
signature_traits.description: "I tried to tune them to the song—whatever would fit in with the song and the way the singer was singing"; tape where the ring was.

patterns.name: Mustang Sally: the groove
patterns.function: The verse and chorus: eighths on the hat with the "and" of 3 open, the snare on 2 and 4, the kick on 1, the "and" of 3 and the "and" of 4.

patterns.name: Respect: the verse
patterns.function: Eighths on the hat with the "and" of 4 open, the snare on 2 and 4, the kick on 1, 3 and its "and".

patterns.name: Chain of Fools: quarters on the hat
patterns.function: Seventy bars unchanged: quarter notes on the hat, the snare on 2 and 4, the kick on 1, 3, its "and" and the "and" of 4.

patterns.name: Chain of Fools: the tom into the chorus
patterns.function: Sixteenths on the high tom on 3 and 4, the backbeat kept, into each chorus.

patterns.name: When a Man Loves a Woman: the 12/8 ride
patterns.function: The verse: the ride in triplets, the snare on pulses 2 and 4, the kick on eighths 1, 6, 7 and 12.

patterns.name: I Never Loved a Man: the shuffle in three
patterns.function: The hat on each beat and its last triplet, the snare on 3, the kick on 1 and the last triplet of 2.

equipment.label: Ludwig, the house kit
equipment.layout_notes: "Most of the time it was Ludwig" (Modern Drummer, 2017); on Traffic's 1973 Musikladen set a black oyster pearl kit with chrome hardware. Sizes and cymbals are not in the sources read.

affiliations.name: Muscle Shoals Rhythm Section
affiliations.notes: FAME's second house band, then owners of Muscle Shoals Sound from 1969; sold in 1985.

affiliations.name: Traffic
affiliations.notes: With Hood and Beckett on the 1973 tour and Shoot Out at the Fantasy Factory.

evidence.note: "Al Jackson was a big influence. I listened to him a lot."

philosophy.idea: Be a listener first: he was a better listener than a drummer.
No tom fills while the singer sings.
Tune the drums to the song and the singer.

innovations: The Muscle Shoals soul backbeat, on hits for Sledge, Pickett and Franklin
Players owning their studio: Muscle Shoals Sound, 1969

accolades.award: Rolling Stone, 100 Greatest Drummers of All Time (2016), no. 31

contribution.description: The Swampers' drummer, whose deep, unhurried feel is on "When a Man Loves a Woman", "Respect" and "Mustang Sally"; Rolling Stone ranked him 31st among the greatest drummers.

beatbreaker.default_kit_sound: A 1960s Ludwig, the snare cracking, taped down
generation_rules: Eighths on the hat with one note opened, the snare on 2 and 4, the kick with the bass.
Fills in the gaps only: a snare roll or a bar of tom into the chorus.
Stops and hits with the band.

lineage_display.lineage_blurb: Al Jackson Jr.'s Stax backbeat, heard and studied, carried to FAME and Muscle Shoals.
